mainTopic: Honoring the dead and the living at funerals, eulogies on חול המועד, and the proper measure of mourning
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about תקנות that keep the poor and the sick from being shamed at death. The plain bier, incense, and immersing utensils were made the same for everyone, and רבן גמליאל's simple linen shrouds ended costly burials. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about not setting the bier down in the street on חול המועד. רב פפא allows a eulogy for a תלמיד חכם in front of the body, and the day the news arrives counts the same as being in front of the body. Next comes a series of mourning teachings: what הספד, טיפוח and קילוס mean, when visitors must leave a mourner, the mourner's first meal, and the town stopping work for a death. רב warns against mourning too much, and a ברייתא sets the limits of 3, 7 and 30 days. The גמרא explains who deserves heavy crying, and רבי לוי describes how a mourner's fear should fade over time. At the end the גמרא goes back to the משנה about women's biers, and the limit from the חכמי נהרדעא continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Everyone is carried out on a plain bier
steps.stepSummary: The poor were shamed by their plain bier, so the חכמים ruled that everyone is buried on a plain bier.
steps.simpleTranslation: The poor were carried out on a plain bier, and they were embarrassed. The חכמים ruled that everyone should be carried out on a plain bier, out of respect for the poor.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its first case. A plain bier had become a sign of being poor, so the חכמים made it the bier for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was the difference between rich and poor at the funeral, not the plain bier itself. The fix brings the rich down to the level of the poor, so nobody can tell who is who. The rest of the ברייתא follows this same pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: A simple bier made of poles tied together
They (the חכמים) made a rule, a תקנה
Out of respect for them, to protect their dignity

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole pattern of the list. When a practice shames one group, the חכמים apply it to everyone.

phrases.english: on a plain bier, and the poor were embarrassed.
phrases.notes: We're joining mid-sentence. Just before this, the ברייתא said the rich were carried on a fancy bed and the poor on this plain bier.

phrases.english: They instituted that everyone should be carried out on a plain bier,
out of respect for the poor.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ הַכֹּל מוֹצִיאִין בִּכְלִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Everyone is carried out for burial on a plain bier, so the poor are not shamed.

steps.title: Incense is placed under every dead person
steps.stepSummary: Incense used to be placed only under people who died of intestinal illness. Now it is placed under everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they placed incense under people who died of intestinal illness, and living people with that illness were embarrassed. The חכמים ruled that incense be placed under everyone, out of respect for the living sick.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second case with the same pattern. Incense had become a public sign of how a person died, so it was made standard for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the people being protected are the living. People who were sick at the time felt shamed knowing they would be marked this way when they died. Using incense for everyone removes that sign.

keyTerms.meaning: Incense, burned to give off a pleasant smell

phrases.english: At first they would place incense
under those who died of an intestinal illness,
and the living who had an intestinal illness were embarrassed.
They instituted that it be placed under everyone,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי כְּבוֹדָן שֶׁל חוֹלֵי מֵעַיִם חַיִּים.
phrases.english: out of respect for the living who had an intestinal illness.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמּוּגְמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list of תקנות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incense is placed under every dead person, so the living sick are not shamed.

steps.title: Utensils are immersed after every woman who dies
steps.stepSummary: Utensils were once immersed only after a woman died as a נדה. Now they are immersed after any woman dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they immersed the utensils used by women who died as נדות, and living נדות were embarrassed. The חכמים ruled that utensils be immersed after all women, out of respect for living נדות.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a third case with the same pattern. Immersing the utensils showed everyone that the woman had died while she was a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing utensils is a real טומאה concern, since a נדה makes utensils טמא. The חכמים did not cancel the immersion. They required it for every woman, so it no longer singles anyone out.

keyTerms.meaning: They immerse in a מקוה to make something טהור
Women in the state of נדה, which causes טומאה
Here: the utensils that were used by

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not say these women were not really נדות. The טומאה rule stays in place. The only change is that the immersion is now done for everyone, so no one can tell.

phrases.english: At first they would immerse the utensils
used by women who died as נדות,
and the living נדות were embarrassed.

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ מַטְבִּילִין עַל גַּבֵּי כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים,
phrases.english: They instituted that they immerse the utensils used by all women,
out of respect for the living נדות.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ מַטְבִּילִין אֶת הַכֵּלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list of תקנות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The utensils of every woman who dies are immersed, so living נדות are not shamed.

steps.title: Utensils are immersed after every man who dies
steps.stepSummary: The same תקנה applies to men: utensils are immersed after every man dies, not only after a זב.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first they immersed the utensils used by men who died as זבין, and living זבין were embarrassed. The חכמים ruled that utensils be immersed after everyone, out of respect for living זבין.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats the last case, this time for men who are זבין. The solution is the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case of זבין matches the case of נדות exactly. Both are people whose טומאה made utensils need immersion. Including both shows that the תקנה covers men as well as women.

keyTerms.meaning: Men with a discharge called זיבה, which makes them טמא

phrases.aramaic: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה מַטְבִּילִין עַל גַּבֵּי זָבִין מֵתִים,
phrases.english: At first they would immerse the utensils used by זבין who died,
and the living זבין were embarrassed.

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ מַטְבִּילִין עַל גַּב הַכֹּל,
phrases.english: They instituted that they immerse the utensils after everyone,
out of respect for the living זבין.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה מַטְבִּילִין עַל גַּבֵּי זָבִין מֵתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 3, applied to men
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The utensils of every man who dies are immersed, so living זבין are not shamed.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל chooses simple linen shrouds
steps.stepSummary: Expensive shrouds made burial so hard that families abandoned their dead. רבן גמליאל was buried in plain linen, and everyone followed him.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first the cost of burying the dead was harder on the relatives than the death itself, until relatives would leave the body and run away. Then רבן גמליאל set aside his own honor and was buried in linen garments, and the people followed him and were buried in linen.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells of one more fix to the burden on poorer families. This time the change came from a great leader's own example, not from a new rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burial clothes had become so costly that families ran away instead of facing the expense. A leader as important as רבן גמליאל chose simple linen for himself. That made simple shrouds respectable, so the poor were no longer shamed or overwhelmed.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying out the dead for burial, including the burial costs
Lightness of head. Here it means giving up his own honor

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the custom to bury every person in simple shrouds.

phrases.english: At first the carrying out of the dead
was harder for his relatives than his death,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁהָיוּ קְרוֹבָיו מַנִּיחִין אוֹתוֹ וּבוֹרְחִין.
phrases.english: until his relatives would leave him and run away.
Until רבן גמליאל came
and treated his own honor lightly,
and was carried out in linen garments,
and the people followed his practice
to be carried out in linen garments.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיְתָה הוֹצָאַת הַמֵּת קָשָׁה לִקְרוֹבָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final item of the ברייתא, this time a change made through personal example
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רבן גמליאל, the dead are buried in simple linen shrouds.

steps.title: רב פפא: today even cheap cloth is used
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds that in his day people were buried in even cheaper cloth worth just a זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: And nowadays everyone's practice is to bury even in a rough cloth that costs a זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא updates the custom from רבן גמליאל's time. In his day, burial clothes had become even simpler and cheaper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Linen was simpler than before, but it still had some cost. רב פפא reports that the trend went further, to cloth worth only a זוז. That made burial affordable for anyone.
steps.whatToRemember: All of these תקנות share one idea. At death, no one should be shamed by poverty or illness, so the practice is made the same, and simple, for everyone.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
And nowadays everyone's practice is
even with rough cloth worth a זוז.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא וְהָאִידָּנָא נְהוּג עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An אמורא's addition updating the custom described in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב פפא's day, the dead were buried even in cheap cloth worth a זוז.

steps.title: The משנה: do not set the bier down in the street
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה about not setting down the bier in the street on חול המועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bier is not set down in the street.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up a discussion. רב פפא's statement in the next step builds on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting the bier down in the street gathers people and starts a public eulogy. The משנה wants to hold back eulogies on חול המועד, so it says not to do this. The next step gives an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: The bier the dead person is carried on
The street or open public square

phrases.english: They do not set down the bier in the street.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, and it is talking about חול המועד.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין מַנִּיחִין אֶת הַמִּטָּה בָּרְחוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the burial shroud discussion to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On חול המועד the bier is not set down in the street, so that a public eulogy does not start.

steps.title: A תלמיד חכם may be eulogized even on חול המועד
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the limits of חול המועד do not apply in front of a תלמיד חכם, and they apply even less on חנוכה and פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: There is no מועד in front of a תלמיד חכם, and all the more so חנוכה and פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives an exception to the משנה's rule. A תלמיד חכם may be eulogized on חול המועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honor of a תלמיד חכם outweighs the usual limit on eulogies during חול המועד. If it is allowed on חול המועד, it is surely allowed on חנוכה and פורים, which are less holy days. That reasoning is a קל וחומר.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival days, here meaning חול המועד
In front of, in the presence of

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
There is no Festival in front of a Torah scholar,
phrases.notes: He means the limits on eulogizing during חול המועד do not apply to a scholar.

phrases.english: and all the more so Hanukkah and Purim.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֵין מוֹעֵד בִּפְנֵי תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an exception to the משנה's limit on eulogies
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם may be eulogized on חול המועד, and surely on חנוכה and פורים.

steps.title: The permission applies only in front of the body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רב פפא's rule: the eulogy is allowed only in front of the deceased.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies only in his presence. When he is not present, it is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows רב פפא's permission. A תלמיד חכם may be eulogized on חול המועד only in front of the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honor of the scholar is strongest when the body is right there. A eulogy held somewhere else does not override חול המועד. This limit sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: These words apply only to..., a limiting phrase
In his presence, in front of the body

phrases.english: And this applies only in his presence,
but not in his presence, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב פפא's permission
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eulogizing a תלמיד חכם on חול המועד is allowed only in front of the body.

steps.title: רב כהנא eulogized רב זביד far from the body
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the limit: רב כהנא eulogized רב זביד in פום נהרא, away from the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב כהנא eulogized רב זביד of נהרדעא in פום נהרא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule from the last step. It brings a story where a scholar was eulogized away from his body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד was from נהרדעא, but רב כהנא eulogized him in פום נהרא, so the body was not there. If only a eulogy in front of the body is allowed, how could רב כהנא do this? The case seems to go against the limit.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? A word that opens a challenge
But look, here is a case that goes against it

phrases.english: Is that so?!
But Rav Kahana eulogized
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes this eulogy happened on חול המועד.

phrases.english: Rav Zevid from Neharde'a
in Pum Nahara!
phrases.notes: That is a different place, so the body was not there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא רַב כָּהֲנָא סַפְדֵיהּ לְרַב זְבִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit from step 9 with a story
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a eulogy on חול המועד is allowed only in front of the body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב כהנא eulogized רב זביד in a different city, away from the body, and it seems that was on חול המועד.

steps.title: The day the news arrives counts as being in front of the body
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי answers that it was the day רב כהנא heard the news, and that day counts as being in his presence.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said: It was the day of the news, and that is like being in his presence.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפי answers the challenge. On the day a person first hears of a death, it is treated as if the body were in front of him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of being 'in his presence' is not only about where the body is. The fresh pain of first hearing the news makes it count the same way. So רב כהנא's eulogy fits the rule, and the limit stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: The day the news of the death arrives
It is considered as if in his presence

steps.whatToRemember: A תלמיד חכם may be eulogized on חול המועד in front of the body. The day the news of his death arrives counts the same as being in front of the body.

phrases.english: Rav Pappi said:
It was the day of the news,
and that is like in his presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פַּפֵּי: יוֹם שְׁמוּעָה הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Widening a definition: 'in his presence' also covers the day the news arrives
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The story seemed to show that a eulogy away from the body is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The day the news arrives counts as being in front of the body, so the limit still stands.

steps.title: עולא defines הספד, טיפוח and קילוס
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains three mourning actions: הספד is striking the heart, טיפוח is clapping the hands, and קילוס is stomping the foot.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: הספד is on the heart, as it is written, 'Striking the breasts.' טיפוח is with the hand. קילוס is with the foot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to explain three mourning words. עולא says which body part each one uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here הספד does not mean a spoken eulogy. It means beating the chest, and עולא brings a פסוק as proof. טיפוח means clapping the hands, and קילוס means stomping the foot.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: striking the chest in mourning

steps.confusionAlert: In this step הספד does not mean a spoken eulogy. עולא means the physical act of beating the chest.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
Hesped is on the heart,
as it is written: "Striking the breasts."
Tipuach is with the hand.
Killus is with the foot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: הֶסְפֵּד עַל לֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: what the mourning actions are
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הספד is beating the chest, טיפוח is clapping the hands, and קילוס is stomping the foot.

steps.title: Stomp in a shoe, not a sandal, because of danger
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone who stomps in mourning should wear a shoe, not a sandal, because a sandal could lead to injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rabbis taught: One who stomps should not stomp in a sandal, but in a shoe, because of the danger.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds a safety rule about קילוס, the stomping that עולא just defined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stomping hard in a sandal can lead to getting hurt, so a shoe should be worn instead. Safety comes first, even while mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: One who stomps his foot in mourning

steps.whatToRemember: קילוס means stomping the foot, and it should be done in a shoe, not a sandal, because of danger.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who stomps should not stomp in a sandal,
but rather in a shoe,
because of the danger.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמְקַלֵּס לֹא יְקַלֵּס בְּסַנְדָּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical rule about קילוס, which עולא just defined
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who stomps in mourning should wear a shoe, not a sandal, because of danger.

steps.title: Visitors leave once the mourner nods his head
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that once an אבל nods his head, the מנחמין may no longer sit beside him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Once a mourner has nodded his head, the comforters are no longer allowed to sit next to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new set of mourning rules from רבי יוחנן. This first one tells visitors when they must get up and leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אבל is in charge of the visit. His nod is a signal, and once he gives it the comforters have no right to keep sitting there. Comforting is meant for the mourner's sake, not the visitor's.

keyTerms.meaning: Comforters, the people who visit to console the mourner

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
A mourner, once he has nodded his head —

phrases.aramaic: שׁוּב אֵין מְנַחֲמִין רַשָּׁאִין לֵישֵׁב אֶצְלוֹ.
phrases.english: the comforters are no longer allowed to sit next to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אָבֵל, כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּיעְנַע רֹאשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the rules about eulogies and mourning gestures to a new set of rulings about how to treat a mourner.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the אבל nods his head, the מנחמין may not stay sitting with him.

steps.title: A mourner and a sick person need not stand for the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that everyone must stand for the נשיא, except an אבל and a חולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Everyone must stand up before the נשיא, except a mourner and a sick person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second ruling: the normal duty to stand for the נשיא does not apply to a mourner or a sick person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing for the leader of the generation is a general duty that falls on everyone. The אבל and the חולה are exceptions, because of their pain and weakness.

keyTerms.meaning: The head of the Sanhedrin, the leader of the generation
To stand up out of respect for someone

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Everyone must stand up before the Nasi,
except a mourner and a sick person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַכֹּל חַיָּיבִין לַעֲמוֹד מִפְּנֵי נָשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from רבי יוחנן about how an אבל is treated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל and a חולה do not have to stand for the נשיא.

steps.title: A mourner and a sick person need not wait to be told to sit
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that everyone who stands must be told 'sit down' before sitting, except an אבל and a חולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: To everyone we say 'Sit down,' except a mourner and a sick person.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds a third ruling that matches the one before it. Normally people wait to be told to sit, but a mourner and a sick person do not have to wait.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said these two do not have to stand. This step says that even if they did stand, they may sit down on their own without waiting for permission. The same two exceptions run through both rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: Sit down! (said to the people standing)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
To everyone we say to them, "Sit down,"
phrases.notes: He means people who stood up for a great person, who normally wait to be told before sitting.

phrases.english: except a mourner and a sick person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לַכֹּל אוֹמְרִים לָהֶם ״שֵׁבוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes along with Step 15 and gives the same two exceptions for sitting back down.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל and a חולה may sit down without being told 'sit.'
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's three rulings all go easy on the mourner. He decides when visitors leave, and he is free from the usual rules of standing and sitting for honor.

steps.title: On the first day a mourner may not eat his own bread
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב rules that an אבל may not eat his own bread on the first day, learned from what the Torah told יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: A mourner on the first day may not eat bread of his own. We know this from what the Merciful One said to יחזקאל: 'And do not eat the bread of men.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: on day one of mourning, the אבל must eat food that others provide. The גמרא brings a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יחזקאל was told not to act like a regular mourner, and one thing he was told not to do was eat 'the bread of men.' This shows that a regular mourner does eat bread from other people, and not his own.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One, meaning ה׳ in the Torah
Bread of men, meaning food brought by other people

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק tells יחזקאל NOT to eat others' bread. That is because he was told not to mourn. So the rule for everyone else is the opposite: a mourner DOES eat others' bread.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
A mourner, on the first day,
is forbidden to eat bread of his own,
since the Merciful One said to Ezekiel:
"And do not eat the bread of men."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: אָבֵל, יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן אָסוּר לֶאֱכוֹל לֶחֶם מִשֶּׁלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of mourning rulings from רב יהודה in the name of רב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the first day, an אבל must eat food given by others, not his own.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the סעודת הבראה, the meal others prepare for the mourner after the burial.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף swapped meals
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף kept the rule by trading meals with each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף would trade their meals with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how two אמוראים kept the rule from Step 17 in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By swapping meals, each one ate bread that was not his own. This shows the rule in practice: the meal only has to come from someone else.

phrases.english: Rabbah and Rav Yosef
would swap their meals with each other.
phrases.notes: This way each ate the other's food, not his own, keeping the rule from Step 17.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף מְחַלְּפִי סְעוֹדָתַיְיהוּ לַהֲדָדֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the rule of Step 17 was kept in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trading meals with another person is enough to keep the rule of not eating one's own bread on the first day.

steps.title: When someone dies in a city, no one there may work
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב rules that when a person dies in a city, all its residents may not do work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: If someone dies in a city, all the people of the city are forbidden to do work.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ruling from רב יהודה in the name of רב. It turns from the mourner himself to the whole town: everyone stops working when someone there dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the rules were about the אבל and his visitors. This ruling puts a duty on the entire city, so that people pay attention to the death and to caring for the dead person.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who died in the city

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:
If someone dies in a city —
all the people of the city
are forbidden to do work.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מֵת בְּעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling from the same chain, רב יהודה in the name of רב, now about the whole community.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When someone dies in a city, all its residents are forbidden to work.

steps.title: רב המנונא sees people working while there is a dead person in town
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא hears the שופר announcing a death, sees people working, and puts them in שמתא for working while there is a dead person in town.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא came to a town called דרומתא. He heard the שופר announcing that someone had died. He saw people working and said: 'Let these people be in שמתא! Isn't there a dead person in town?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that puts the rule from step 19 into action. רב המנונא punishes people for working while a dead person is in town. The next step gives their answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 19 taught that when someone dies in a city, all the residents may not do work. רב המנונא treats this as a serious obligation, serious enough to put people in שמתא. His question 'isn't there a dead person in town?!' sets up the people's reply.

keyTerms.meaning: shofar (here blown to announce a death)
a dead person (literally, 'one who lies down')

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna happened to come to Darumata,
he heard the sound of the shofar for a dead person.

phrases.aramaic: חֲזָא הָנָךְ אִינָשֵׁי דְּקָא עָבְדִי עֲבִידְתָּא,
phrases.english: He saw some people who were doing work,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לֶיהְווֹ הָנָךְ אִינָשֵׁי בְּשַׁמְתָּא.
phrases.english: he said to them: Let these people be in excommunication.
Is there not a dead person in the town?!
phrases.notes: He is relying on the rule from the step before this: when someone dies in town, nobody may work.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הַמְנוּנָא אִיקְּלַע לְדֵרוּ מָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that applies the rule of step 19 in real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Doing work in a town while a dead person is there is serious enough to deserve שמתא.

steps.title: Separate groups in town make the work permitted
steps.stepSummary: The people explain that the town has separate groups, each handling its own dead, so רב המנונא permits their work.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: 'There are separate groups in the town.' He said to them: 'If so, it is permitted for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The townspeople answer רב המנונא's challenge. He accepts the answer and cancels the ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of step 19 assumes the whole town is involved with the dead. When a town is divided into groups that each care for their own dead, the members of other groups are not bound. This step marks a limit on the rule. It does not cancel the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: groups (each in charge of its own members' dead)

steps.whatToRemember: A whole town stops work for a death only when the town functions as one community. If it is split into separate burial groups, other groups may keep working.

phrases.english: They said to him: There are groups in the town.
phrases.notes: Each group took care of its own dead, and the person who died was not from their group.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אִי הָכִי, שַׁרְיָא לְכוּ.
phrases.english: He said to them: If so, it is permitted to you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: חֲבוּרָתָא אִיכָּא בְּמָתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב המנונא's challenge and limits the rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the rule applies only when the town is one community.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any death in town forbids all residents from working.
steps.terutzMaskana: When there are separate groups, only the dead person's group stops work.

steps.title: Grieving too much leads to crying over another death
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב: whoever grieves over his dead more than is proper will end up crying over another dead person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: Anyone who grieves too much over his dead will end up crying over another dead person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רב יהודה in the name of רב. It warns against mourning too much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was how much mourning is required. Here the topic turns around: there is also a limit on how much one should mourn. Mourning past that limit is treated as dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: one who grieves heavily, takes it very hard

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַמִּתְקַשֶּׁה עַל מֵתוֹ יוֹתֵר מִדַּאי,
phrases.english: Anyone who grieves over his dead too much,
will be crying over another dead person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כׇּל הַמִּתְקַשֶּׁה עַל מֵתוֹ יוֹתֵר מִדַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the limits on mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grieving too much brings more grief.

steps.title: The woman who mourned her son too much
steps.stepSummary: A woman near רב הונא kept crying too much over one of her seven sons. She ignored his warnings, all her sons died, and then she died too.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman lived in רב הונא's neighborhood and had seven sons. One died, and she cried over him too much. רב הונא sent her a message: 'Don't do this!' She ignored him. He sent again: 'If you listen, good. If not, prepare shrouds for the next one to die.' They all died. In the end he told her: 'Prepare shrouds for yourself,' and she died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows רב's warning coming true. A woman ignores רב הונא's warnings against mourning too much, and the deaths keep coming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא warns her twice, and each time she ignores him, the result gets worse. Her too-much crying leads to more deaths, exactly as רב said: 'he will cry over another dead person.'

keyTerms.meaning: provisions for a journey; here, burial shrouds

steps.confusionAlert: This story does not mean we should not mourn. Mourning itself is required. The warning is only against mourning past the proper limits, which the next step spells out.

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּהֲוָת בְּשִׁיבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: There was a certain woman who lived in Rav Huna's neighborhood,
she had seven sons,
one of them died,
and she was crying over him excessively.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לַהּ רַב הוּנָא: לָא תַּעַבְדִי הָכִי!
phrases.english: Rav Huna sent to her: Don't do this!
She paid no attention to him.
He sent to her: If you listen, good,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא — צְבִית זְוַודְתָּא לְאִידַּךְ מִית,
phrases.english: and if not, prepare shrouds for the other one who will die,
And they all died.
In the end he said to her:
Prepare shrouds for yourself, and she died.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּהֲוָת בְּשִׁיבָבוּתֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that illustrates and backs up רב's warning.
steps.raayaObject: רב's statement that grieving too much leads to crying over another death.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of the woman in רב הונא's neighborhood.

steps.title: A verse sets fixed limits for mourning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'weep not for the dead, nor bemoan him' as forbidding too much mourning, and sets the limits: 3 days of crying, 7 of הספד, and 30 days of no ironing or haircuts. Beyond that, הקדוש ברוך הוא says: you are not more merciful than Me.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Weep not for the dead, nor bemoan him.' 'Weep not for the dead' means not too much. 'Nor bemoan him' means not longer than the proper amount. How so? Three days for crying, seven for הספד, and thirty for not ironing and not cutting hair. From then on, הקדוש ברוך הוא says: You are not more merciful to him than I am.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק that gives a Torah source for limiting mourning. It then spells out exactly how long each stage of mourning should last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not read the פסוק as 'don't mourn at all.' It reads it as 'don't mourn too much or too long.' It then gives clear measures: 3, 7, and 30 days. Mourning beyond these measures is like claiming to be more merciful than הקדוש ברוך הוא.

keyTerms.meaning: bemoan, shake the head in grief

steps.whatToRemember: Mourning has set stages: 3 days of crying, 7 days of הספד, and 30 days of no ironing and no haircuts. Going beyond them is too much.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא gives the basic time frames of אבלות that הלכה follows, and it explains why mourning must stop at a certain point.

phrases.english: "Weep not for the dead, nor bemoan him."
"Weep not for the dead" means too much,
"nor bemoan him" means more than the proper amount.
How so?
Three days for crying, and seven for eulogizing,
and thirty for ironing and haircutting.

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ — אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: From here on, the Holy One, Blessed be He, says:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתֶּם רַחְמָנִים בּוֹ יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנִּי.
phrases.english: You are not more merciful to him than I am.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַל תִּבְכּוּ לְמֵת וְאַל תָּנוּדוּ לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as the source for limiting mourning, and sets exact limits.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mourning is limited to 3 days of crying, 7 days of הספד, and 30 days of no ironing and no haircuts. Mourning beyond that is too much.

steps.title: Real crying is for the one who dies without children
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק continues 'weep sore for the one who goes away.' רב יהודה explains that this means one who dies without children.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Weep sore for the one who goes away.' רב יהודה said: This means one who goes away without children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at the next part of the same פסוק. That part tells us to cry hard, and רב יהודה explains who it is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק limited crying. The second half asks for heavy crying for 'the one who goes away.' רב יהודה says this is a person who leaves the world with no children to carry on after him.

keyTerms.meaning: for the one who goes away

phrases.english: "Weep sore for the one who goes away,"
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק in ירמיהו.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לַהוֹלֵךְ בְּלֹא בָּנִים.
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: For one who goes away without children.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכוּ בָכוֹ לַהוֹלֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of the פסוק from step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'The one who goes away' who deserves heavy crying is one who dies without children.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי visited mourners only for the childless
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי went to a house of mourning only when the dead person had no children, based on the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי would go to a house of mourning only for someone who died without children, as it says: 'Weep sore for the one who goes away, for he will not return again and see his native land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows a great אמורא acting on רב יהודה's explanation. He saved his mourning visits for people who died childless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי's practice supports reading 'the one who goes away' as someone who died childless. The rest of the פסוק, 'he will not return,' fits a person who leaves nothing of himself behind.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לָא אֲזַל לְבֵי אִבְלָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi would not go to a house of mourning
except for one who went away without children,
as it is written: "Weep sore for the one who goes away,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי לֹא יָשׁוּב עוֹד וְרָאָה אֶת אֶרֶץ מוֹלַדְתּוֹ״.
phrases.english: for he will not return again and see his native land."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לָא אֲזַל לְבֵי אִבְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practice that follows רב יהודה's reading.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's reading that 'the one who goes away' means one who dies childless.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי's practice of visiting mourners only in that case.

steps.title: רב הונא: the one who goes away is a repeat sinner
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains 'the one who goes away' differently: a person who sinned and then repeated the sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: This means a person who did a sin and then did it again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of 'the one who goes away.' רב הונא disagrees with רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, the heavy crying is not about having no children. It is about a person who keeps repeating a sin. 'He will not return' then means he does not come back in תשובה, so he loses his true 'homeland.'
steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of 'weep sore for the one who goes away.' רב יהודה says it is one who dies childless. רב הונא says it is one who keeps repeating a sin.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
This is one who did a sin and repeated it.
phrases.notes: He reads 'he will not return' as a person who keeps sinning and never comes back in תשובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: זֶה שֶׁעָבַר עֲבֵירָה וְשָׁנָה בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same words that רב יהודה explained in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'The one who goes away' is someone who sinned and repeated the sin.

steps.title: רב הונא's view matches another teaching of his
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב הונא's reading of the פסוק fits his known teaching that a sin repeated becomes 'permitted' to the sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא is following his own reasoning. He said elsewhere: once a person sins and repeats the sin, it becomes permitted to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא read 'the one who goes away' as someone who sinned twice. He has another teaching about how repeating a sin changes a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 27, רב הונא said the person we should cry for is the one who sinned and repeated it. Here the גמרא shows the reason: a repeated sin makes a person comfortable with sinning, so he may never come back. That is why he is truly 'going away.'

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning (consistent with his other teachings)

phrases.english: Rav Huna follows his own reasoning,
phrases.notes: This links back to רב הונא's reading of 'the one who goes away' in the previous step.

phrases.english: for Rav Huna said:
once a person commits a sin
and repeats it,
it becomes permitted to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב הונא's reading of the פסוק in Step 27 by showing it matches his other teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's reading of 'the one who goes away' as a repeat sinner
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's own teaching that a repeated sin becomes 'permitted' to the sinner

steps.title: Can a sin really become permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording: how could a sin ever actually become permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It becomes permitted to him'? Can you really think that?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the words 'it becomes permitted.' A sin cannot actually become allowed just because someone did it twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, רב הונא's words would mean repeating a sin makes it allowed. That is impossible, so the wording has to be fixed. This sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (meaning: that can't be right)

phrases.english: "Permitted to him" — could that enter your mind?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּתְּרָה לוֹ סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal wording of רב הונא's teaching quoted in Step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'הותרה לו' in רב הונא's teaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sin can never become permitted according to הלכה just because it was repeated, so the words cannot be meant literally.

steps.title: It only feels permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: the sin becomes 'like' something permitted in the sinner's eyes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: it becomes to him like something permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording. The sin is still forbidden, but to the sinner it now feels like it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change from 'permitted' to 'like permitted' moves the teaching from the הלכה to the person's mind. After doing a sin twice, he no longer feels its seriousness. That is the danger רב הונא was describing.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (the wording is being corrected)

steps.whatToRemember: A sin never becomes permitted. But after repeating it, a person starts to feel as if it is permitted, and that is why he is 'going away.'

phrases.english: Rather, say:
it becomes to him like something permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: נַעֲשֵׂית לוֹ כְּהֶיתֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 29 by correcting the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words seemed to say that the sin actually becomes allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sin only feels allowed to the person who keeps doing it.

steps.title: How a mourner should feel in the days after the death
steps.stepSummary: רבי לוי describes three stages of fear for an אבל: a sword between his thighs, a sword in the corner, and a sword passing in the market.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי לוי said: In the first three days, an אבל should see himself as if a sword is lying between his thighs. From the third to the seventh day, as if it is lying in the corner facing him. From then on, as if it is passing in front of him in the market.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי לוי gives a picture of how an אבל should feel. The sense that danger is close should be strongest at first and get weaker with time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sword stands for danger and the reminder of death. In the first 3 days it is right on him, from day 3 to 7 it is in the room, and after that it is only passing by. This matches the stages of mourning from Step 24: 3 days, then 7, then after.

phrases.english: Rabbi Levi said:
A mourner, during the first three days,
should see himself
as if a sword is lying
between his two thighs.
From the third to the seventh day,
as if it is lying opposite him
in the corner.
From then on,
as if it is passing in front of him in the marketplace.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי לֵוִי: אָבֵל, שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about mourning that matches the 3-day and 7-day stages from Step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אבל should feel danger very close for 3 days, somewhat close until day 7, and far off after that.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: women's biers are never set down
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that a woman's bier is never set down, out of respect, and the חכמי נהרדעא begin to limit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And those of women are never set down, out of respect.' The Sages of נהרדעא said: They only taught this...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quote another line from the משנה. Then it starts the חכמי נהרדעא's limit on that rule, which continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a woman's bier is never set down in the street, to protect her honor. 'לא שנו' means 'they only taught this in a certain case,' so a limit on the rule is coming. The exact limit comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Out of respect / for her honor
